reason: The cited lines show the tool sends a user-supplied URL and options to a fixed Firecrawl API endpoint and returns the crawl result. They do not show arbitrary code execution on the host. They do not establish access to non-public/local/intranet/user-credentialed data, though the broader tool might have options not shown, so SECRET is not settled. SINK is supported because, when not in safe mode, the schema accepts `webhook` and `webhookHeaders` and the options are spread into the crawl request, enabling delivery to a caller/agent-specified webhook destination. UNTRUSTED is supported because the returned crawl/page data comes from a user-supplied URL and can be attacker-controlled.
